proposals.name: pytest-coverage
proposals.listing_description: Annotated pytest coverage workflow for locating missing lines and iterating toward complete line coverage.
proposals.use_when: A Python pytest suite needs an annotated coverage report and tests for specific missing lines.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The task is JavaScript unit testing, browser E2E, or only a build configuration failure.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: No host-specific tool is required; retain pytest commands as written.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Provide the annotated pytest coverage workflow with the host's ordinary command runner.
unchanged_technical_points: The goal is to cover all source lines.
Run pytest --cov --cov-report=annotate:cov_annotate.
Optionally scope with --cov=module or a specific test file while retaining the annotate report.
Inspect cov_annotate, with one annotated file per source file.
Do not open files reported at 100%; inspect matching files below 100%.
A line beginning ! is uncovered; add tests for missing lines and repeat until all lines are covered.

proposals.name: javascript-typescript-jest
proposals.listing_description: Jest guidance for structured JavaScript and TypeScript unit tests, mocks, asynchronous assertions, snapshots, and common matchers.
proposals.use_when: An existing JavaScript or TypeScript implementation needs Jest unit tests, mocks or async assertions.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The request is browser E2E, Python coverage, or production logic is still undefined.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the host's JavaScript test runner label while retaining Jest API names.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Guide a Jest test implementation using the repository's test-file layout and available host runner.
unchanged_technical_points: Use .test.ts or .test.js files next to code or in __tests__, descriptive names, nested describe blocks, and the describe/it pattern.
Mock external dependencies with jest.mock, jest.spyOn, mockImplementation or mockReturnValue, and reset with jest.resetAllMocks in afterEach.
Return promises or use async/await; use resolves/rejects and set jest.setTimeout for slow tests.
Keep snapshots small and focused and review snapshot changes; for React use React Testing Library, user behavior, accessibility queries, and userEvent over fireEvent.
Retain the listed Jest matcher families for equality, truthiness, numbers, strings, arrays, objects, exceptions, and mock calls.

proposals.name: temporal-python-testing
proposals.listing_description: Temporal Python testing guidance with pytest, time-skipping, activity isolation, integration coverage, and replay determinism.
proposals.use_when: Temporal Python workflows need pytest time-skipping, activity isolation or replay determinism testing.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The application does not use Temporal, or the request is ordinary pytest coverage without workflow history.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Replace only host references for loading progressive resources; preserve Temporal and pytest names.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Apply the Temporal workflow-testing guide and load the relevant frozen resource for unit, integration, local setup, or replay work.
unchanged_technical_points: Use pytest async fixtures, time-skipping, mocked activities, replay determinism, and mostly integration tests; distinguish unit, integration, and sparing end-to-end tests.
Progressively load unit-testing, integration-testing, replay-testing, or local-setup resources according to the testing need.
WorkflowEnvironment.start_time_skipping with Worker and ActivityEnvironment are the basic workflow and activity patterns; cover workflows and activities at the stated 80% target.
Use time-skipping, manual time advancement, isolated activities, shared fixtures, parameterization, retries, error cases, and deterministic feedback.

Replay testing re-executes histories with Replayer, checks deterministic decisions, supports multiple histories, exported files, CI integration, version compatibility with workflow.get_version, and avoids random(), datetime.now(), and direct external calls.

The imported unit-testing resource covers WorkflowEnvironment, ActivityEnvironment, fast long-running tests, manual advancement, pytest fixtures, and patterns; the imported replay-testing resource covers history replay, determinism, CI, compatibility, and history export.

proposals.name: csharp-mstest
proposals.listing_description: MSTest 3.x/4.x practices for unit-test structure, modern assertions, lifecycle, data-driven tests, and test context.
proposals.use_when: A C# project explicitly uses MSTest for unit or data-driven tests.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The project uses pytest, Jest, Playwright or Spring/JUnit.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the host's .NET test command label; preserve dotnet test and MSTest API names.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Guide a C# MSTest suite using the project's existing test-project conventions and host command runner.
unchanged_technical_points: Use a separate [ProjectName].Tests project, MSTest 3.x+ packages, optionally MSTest.Sdk, and dotnet test.
Use sealed [TestClass] classes, [TestMethod], AAA, descriptive MethodName_Scenario_ExpectedBehavior names, constructors for setup, cleanup attributes, and the documented execution order.
Retain modern Assert, StringAssert, CollectionAssert, exception, comparison, type, and Assert.That APIs; prefer Assert.Throws over ExpectedException.
Use DataRow and prefer typed ValueTuple or TestDataRow DynamicData over object arrays.
Use TestContext property or constructor injection, cancellation tokens with Timeout, output/result files, retry, OS/CI conditions, parallelization, and work-item traceability as applicable.
Follow the listed mistake avoidance, test organization, analyzer, and Moq/NSubstitute isolation guidance.

proposals.name: github-actions-efficiency
proposals.listing_description: Evidence-led GitHub Actions workflow efficiency audit covering runtime, caching, triggers, concurrency, matrices, and validation.
proposals.use_when: GitHub Actions workflow duration, caching or redundant CI work needs optimization.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The immediate gap is a test procedure, browser scenario or local assertion.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the host shell and CI command labels; retain rg, gh, and workflow concepts.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Audit workflows from repository files and available run evidence, then recommend and validate only supported efficiency fixes.
unchanged_technical_points: If workflows are absent, load the actions reference and define a baseline; if shell or gh is unavailable, request workflow and recent-run contents and label the result static-only.
Measure triggers, paths, strategy/matrix, cache, recent runs, and failed logs; look for cache gaps, missing cancellation, broad triggers, duplicate coverage, and expensive unconditional jobs.

Apply guardrails: retain required validation, justify parallelism changes, preserve documented matrix legs, flag automatic write-back jobs for opt-in triggers, and separate repo YAML from org settings.

Select up to three evidence-supported fixes from lockfile caching, concurrency cancellation, duplicate coverage removal, safe trigger narrowing, matrix reduction, and independent-job parallelization, ranked by daily minutes saved.
Validate live with a non-protected test push when gh is available; otherwise state what was local-only, and report waste sources, fixes, validation, and measured versus expected impact.

proposals.name: breakdown-test
proposals.listing_description: Comprehensive QA planning prompt for test strategy, task breakdown, quality gates, issues, dependencies, and metrics.
proposals.use_when: An existing broad test must be decomposed into smaller focused test cases.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The task is to discover missing coverage, explore a browser or choose a testing framework.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use repository-specific documentation and issue-system labels without changing QA terminology.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Generate the three requested QA planning documents from the supplied feature artifacts, retaining the framework and quality-gate structure.
unchanged_technical_points: Require PRD, technical breakdown, implementation plan, and GitHub project plan inputs.
Produce test strategy, test issues checklist, and QA plan at the documented paths.
Apply ISTQB activities and design techniques, functional/non-functional/structural/change-related test types, risk-based testing, and ISO 25010 characteristics.
Cover environment and data strategy, tools, CI/CD, test-level and task-level issues, estimates, dependencies, sequencing, assignment, and quality metrics.

Include quality gates, entry/exit criteria, escalation, issue template compliance, labels, priorities, dependency validation, estimation review, and the specified coverage, defect, performance, accessibility, and security targets.

proposals.name: playwright-generate-test
proposals.listing_description: Scenario-first Playwright test generation after completing each prescribed browser interaction.
proposals.use_when: A supplied browser scenario must be explored step by step before emitting a passing Playwright TypeScript test.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The request is unit testing, coverage-only work, or no browser scenario is provided.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Translate only the browser automation host label; preserve Playwright MCP references where they are technical requirements.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Complete the supplied browser scenario step by step, then save and run the resulting @playwright/test TypeScript file in tests.
unchanged_technical_points: Ask for a scenario when none is provided.
Do not generate code prematurely; run each scenario step using the provided browser automation service.
Only after all steps emit a Playwright TypeScript test using @playwright/test, save it in tests, execute it, and iterate until it passes.

proposals.name: scoutqa-test
proposals.listing_description: Exploratory web QA workflow for smoke tests, accessibility, user flows, issue extraction, and result reporting.
proposals.use_when: A web application needs exploratory QA, accessibility auditing or user-flow verification.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The request is a deterministic unit test, code coverage report or non-browser build failure.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the host's background-command and browser-report labels; preserve scoutqa command syntax.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Write a goal-oriented exploratory prompt, start the remote web QA run, capture its identifiers, and report analyzed issues with severity and location.
unchanged_technical_points: Use the workflow: write a specific prompt, run scoutqa in background with a five-second command timeout, tell the user the execution and browser URLs, then extract and analyze results.
Prompts describe goals rather than prescriptive steps and may cover authentication, core workflows, accessibility, forms, responsiveness, smoke tests, or feature verification.
Support localhost URLs, optional project association, verbose output, issue listing by execution, issue verification, and follow-up messages for stuck runs.
Final reports include execution ID, each issue's severity/category/impact/location, and a concise summary; use cleanup and graceful timeout guidance.

proposals.name: spring-boot-testing
proposals.listing_description: Spring Boot 4 testing guidance for narrow test slices, AssertJ assertions, modern APIs, coverage, and maintainable test organization.
proposals.use_when: A Spring Boot application needs the narrowest appropriate JUnit test slice and meaningful assertions.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The project is Python or TypeScript, or the failure is solely CI infrastructure.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the host's Java build command label while preserving Spring, JUnit, AssertJ, and annotation names.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Select the narrowest Spring test style for the behavior, use modern Spring Boot 4 APIs and AssertJ, and organize tests by scenario and risk.
unchanged_technical_points: Follow the pyramid unit > slice > integration, narrowest-confidence, AssertJ, MockMvcTester, and RestTestClient principles.
Select @WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest, @RestClientTest, @JsonTest, or @SpringBootTest for the corresponding scenario; use the listed reference materials.
Use the Spring Boot 4 highlights RestTestClient, @MockitoBean, MockMvcTester, modular starters, and context pausing.
Refactor methods needing more than 5-7 cases, avoid redundancy, use descriptive @DisplayName, order happy path/alternatives/errors, and test production scenarios.
Aim for 80% meaningful coverage with Jacoco, prioritize critical/complex/error/integration paths, and retain the listed test, web, and Testcontainers dependencies.

proposals.name: playwright-explore-website
proposals.listing_description: Browser exploration workflow that identifies core flows, records locators and outcomes, and proposes tests.
proposals.use_when: A site must be interactively explored and documented without yet generating a durable E2E test.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The scenario and desired artifact are already a Playwright test file or a unit test.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the host browser automation label without changing the interaction and locator requirements.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Explore the supplied site, document three to five core flows with UI locators and outcomes, close the browser, summarize findings, and propose tests.
unchanged_technical_points: Navigate to the provided URL and ask for one if absent.
Identify and interact with 3-5 core features or user flows.
Document interactions, relevant UI elements and locators, expected outcomes, a concise summary, and proposed test cases.
Close the browser context on completion.

proposals.name: webapp-testing
proposals.listing_description: Local web-application browser testing for functionality, debugging, screenshots, console logs, and responsive behavior.
proposals.use_when: A general web application test plan or interaction smoke test is requested.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The task requires a specific pytest, Jest, Spring or frozen Playwright procedure.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the available browser automation host or local Node.js fallback; retain Playwright API names.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Verify a running local web application through browser interactions and observable outputs, capturing diagnostics and cleaning up resources.
unchanged_technical_points: Prefer the browser automation service and fall back to local Node.js with Playwright when unavailable; require Node.js, an accessible app, and Playwright.
Support navigation, clicks, form fills, dropdowns, dialogs, presence/text/visibility/URL assertions, responsive checks, screenshots, console logs, network inspection, and failed-test debugging.
Always verify the app is running, use explicit waits, capture failure screenshots, close resources, handle timeouts, and test incrementally.
Prefer data-testid or role selectors and retain the wait, existence, console, and error-handling patterns; do not claim native mobile support.

proposals.name: react19-test-patterns
proposals.listing_description: React 19 test migration patterns for act imports, event simulation, StrictMode counts, and async warnings.
proposals.use_when: React 19 component behavior needs framework-specific test patterns.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The target is a non-React Jest library, Python package or browser journey.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the host test command label only; retain React, RTL, and npm command semantics.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Migrate React tests in the prescribed dependency order and measure, rather than guess, StrictMode call counts.
unchanged_technical_points: Fix act import from react-dom/test-utils to react first.
Replace Simulate with fireEvent and renderIntoDocument with render from @testing-library/react; remove remaining test-utils APIs using the mapping.
Measure React 19 StrictMode effect call counts from the failing test, update effect assertions to one call, retain two calls for render-phase calls, then address async act warnings.
Verify a custom render helper once per codebase rather than per test.

proposals.name: unit-test-vue-pinia
proposals.listing_description: Behavior-first Vue 3, TypeScript, Vitest, and Pinia unit-test guidance with focused stores, components, and composables.
proposals.use_when: Vue code with Pinia stores needs focused unit tests.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The project uses Jest without Vue, Playwright E2E, pytest or Spring Boot.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the host's JavaScript test command label; retain Vitest, Pinia, and Vue Test Utils API names.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Choose the narrowest Vue behavior boundary, configure the least powerful Pinia setup, drive public inputs, and assert observable outputs.
unchanged_technical_points: Identify component, composable, or store behavior; use one behavior per test and black-box observable assertions before instance assertions.
Prefer explicit beforeEach setup, reset mocks, checked-in Pinia patterns, createTestingPinia with createSpy: vi.fn for component tests, and stubActions according to need.
Use initialState and plugins when needed, getter overrides only for edge cases, createPinia for pure store transitions, and real actions only when side effects require them.
Mount shallow by default, drive props/forms/clicks/emits/store APIs, use nextTick only for async updates, assert emitted payloads, and reserve wrapper.vm for exceptions.
Keep fixtures deterministic, avoid private details and excessive snapshots, and flag coverage gaps, brittle selectors, and coupled assertions.

proposals.name: azure-deployment-preflight
proposals.listing_description: Azure Bicep preflight validation for syntax, what-if changes, permissions, parameters, and a Markdown report.
proposals.use_when: An Azure deployment needs subscription, resource and configuration preflight checks.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The failure is a local test, coverage gap or browser flow.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the host shell's Azure command labels while retaining az, azd, and bicep commands.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Detect azd or az workflow, locate Bicep and parameters, validate syntax, run scope-appropriate what-if with fallback, and write the required report.
unchanged_technical_points: Detect azure.yaml for azd, locate Bicep under infra or common locations, and auto-detect .bicepparam, .parameters.json, parameters.json, or environment parameters.
Run bicep build --stdout; capture errors, warnings, and status, noting missing CLI while continuing.
Use azd provision --preview for azd projects; otherwise inspect targetScope and use group/sub/mg/tenant what-if with Provider validation and ProviderNoRbac fallback for permission errors.
Classify create/delete/modify/no-change/ignore/deploy results and capture modified properties.

Generate project-root preflight-report.md with summary, tools, issues, what-if results, and recommendations; gather resource group, subscription, location, and environment as required, and check tool availability.

proposals.name: creating-oracle-to-postgres-migration-integration-tests
proposals.listing_description: Phase-3 Oracle integration-test creation for portable data-access behavior, collision-safe seeds, deterministic assertions, and rollback.
proposals.use_when: Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration integration tests must be implemented.
proposals.do_not_use_when: No database migration exists, or the task is unit coverage or browser E2E.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the host's .NET test command label without changing Oracle, PostgreSQL, or transaction terminology.
proposals.adapted_proposal: For Phase 3 only, inspect one existing Oracle test project, seed minimal records, write portable integration cases, and review determinism before migration.
unchanged_technical_points: Require an existing compiling test project and read its base test class and seed conventions.

Discover conventions, identify database-touching repositories/DAOs/procedure callers/query builders, create minimal collision-safe seeds without TRUNCATE, avoid committing seeds, and use transaction rollback.
Load and verify seeds; create or reuse LookupConstants for stable lookup identifiers.
Inherit the base class, cover each in-scope database method, assert logical concrete outputs rather than platform messages or non-null values, and avoid impossible/redundant cases.
Where applicable cover empty and NULL text, and datetime round trips at the Oracle column precision; review every assertion for deterministic seeded behavior.
Keep the work scoped to Phase 3 Oracle as the golden source, not Phase 6 PostgreSQL.

proposals.name: planning-oracle-to-postgres-migration-integration-testing
proposals.listing_description: Single-project Oracle-to-PostgreSQL integration-test planning for data-access artifacts, migration risks, seeds, and coverage mapping.
proposals.use_when: An Oracle-to-PostgreSQL integration testing migration plan is needed before implementation.
proposals.do_not_use_when: The task is a current test failure, ordinary coverage work or browser exploration.
proposals.host_tool_name_adaptation: Use the host documentation and issue-path labels while preserving the required report path and database terminology.
proposals.adapted_proposal: Analyze one project, rank database touchpoints by migration risk, and write the prescribed integration-testing plan.
unchanged_technical_points: Identify repositories, DAOs, stored procedure callers, and service CRUD methods that directly interact with the database, within one target project.
Classify risk and prioritize Oracle-specific refcursors, TO_CHAR, implicit coercion, and NO_DATA_FOUND over simple CRUD.
Write the Markdown plan to .github/oracle-to-postgres-migration/Reports/{TARGET_PROJECT} Integration Testing Plan.md.
Include artifact method signatures, cases, seed requirements, Oracle-to-PostgreSQL differences, and coverage mapping for every database touchpoint.
Explicitly cover empty and NULL text, datetime/timezone round trips and comparisons, timestamp without time zone or timestamp(0), and timezone-application expectations.
Keep single-project/database-only scope, Oracle as golden source, and no multi-connection harnessing.
